title: Patron of ecology (1979)
hook: John Paul II names Francis patron of those who care for creation

segments.voice: Yesterday, the Capuchins: a reform in long hoods that went back to Francis's poverty. Your line was the hooded friars. Whose heavy story did you hear all the way to the end? Day one thousand two hundred twenty-four.

Brother Sun. Sister Moon and the stars. Brother Wind. Sister Water. Brother Fire. It sounds like a roll call at a very large family reunion, and in a way it is. These are the names Francis gives the world in a song he wrote in his own Italian dialect, the Canticle of the Creatures. Tradition says he made it near the end of his life, sick, in pain, his eyes so bad he could barely stand the light. A man who could hardly see the sun called it his brother. Centuries later, a pope looked at that song and gave Francis a new job. Today's word is the job.
screen: `BROTHER SUN. SISTER MOON.` → `A SONG FROM A SICK MAN.` → `A NEW JOB FOR FRANCIS.`

segments.voice: Pope John Paul II named Francis the patron of those who care for creation, the patron of ecology. A patron, for Catholics, is a saint in heaven asked to pray for a particular people or work. So anyone who plants a tree or cleans a river has, in Catholic eyes, a friend in brown. Why Francis? Because of the Canticle. Listen to what it does. It praises God for the sun, who brings the day and is beautiful and radiant. For the wind and the air and every kind of weather. For water, useful and humble and precious and pure. For fire, bright and strong, who lights the night. And then for the earth, and here is the surprise. Francis doesn't call the earth brother. He calls her our sister and our mother, who feeds us and brings forth fruit and colored flowers and grass. Our line today says brother earth, and that's on purpose: it borrows the family word, not the exact one. The point is kinship. For Francis, creation isn't scenery or stuff. It is family, all of it singing back to the one who made it. The Bible gives the same job from the very start. In Genesis, in the Douay-Rheims, God takes the man and puts him in the garden "to dress it, and to keep it." Not to own it. To tend it and guard it. And the book of Daniel has a whole song where every creature is invited to join in: "All ye works of the Lord, bless the Lord." A patron of ecology, then, is not a saint of recycling bins. He's a saint who heard the world praying, and took his place in the choir.
screen: `A PATRON PRAYS FOR A PEOPLE OR A WORK.` · `SUN, WIND, WATER, FIRE: ALL PRAISE.` · `EARTH: OUR SISTER AND OUR MOTHER.` · `TO DRESS IT AND TO KEEP IT.` · then, large: `ALL YE WORKS OF THE LORD, BLESS THE LORD.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: pick up litter. If you can step outside, do it now. Walk a few steps, find three pieces of trash, a wrapper, a bottle cap, a receipt, and pick them up. Carry them to a bin. If you can't go out, look around the room you're in and clear one small mess, or name the street corner you'll tend later today. As you do it, notice what you're handling: a small corner of the earth Francis called sister and mother. If you pray, you can thank God for one creature you can see right now. The bell holds the time.
Patron of ecology. Francis, named by a pope as the saint who prays for those who care for creation, because he sang about the sun and the earth as family. Today's word.

Your line: brother earth. Today, call one thing in nature by a family name, out loud or in your head, the rain, a tree, the moon, and see if you treat it differently. Day one thousand two hundred twenty-four.

howItsDone: Catholics keep the feast of Saint Francis in early October, and some parishes bless animals on or near that day; Catholic groups who work for the care of creation often take Francis as their patron.

what it means: a saint asked to pray for those who care for creation, because he saw sun, water, fire and earth as family praising God.
what a scholar hears: in the Canticle, Francis's little word per can be read 'for', 'by' or 'through': praised be my Lord for, or through, sister water. readers still weigh each one.

notes: The index carry is 'brother earth', but the Canticle calls the earth 'sora nostra matre terra' (our sister, Mother Earth). The script keeps the carry exactly and says openly that the line borrows the family word, not Francis's exact one. A Keeper may wish to change the outline carry to 'sister earth' (separate, owner-approved edit).
Claims rule: the title's date (1979, the bull Inter Sanctos) is not repeated in the voice. Confirm the paraphrase 'patron of those who care for creation / patron of ecology'.

Canticle paraphrased (no pre-1929 translation on the public-domain list). Confirm the adjectives: sun beautiful and radiant; water useful, humble, precious and chaste ('pure' used); fire bright/beautiful, robust and strong, lighting the night; earth who sustains and governs us and brings forth fruit with colored flowers and herbs.
'Tradition says he made it near the end of his life, sick and nearly blind' follows Franciscan sources (composed at San Damiano c. 1225). Confirm.
Trapdoor: the ambiguity of 'per' (for/by/through) in the Canticle is a common point in Franciscan scholarship; confirm the wording.
Douay-Rheims wording to confirm: Genesis 2:15 ('to dress it, and to keep it') and Daniel 3:57.
howItsDone: the feast (4 October) and the blessing of animals are given without a date in the voice; confirm 'some parishes'.
